selected_mechanism.name: Railbelt LNG-Import Fuel Gate for AI Data-Center Power

news_trigger.what_happened: The Regulatory Commission of Alaska is concerned that customers will end up stuck paying unreasonably inflated infrastructure costs to construct multiple facilities for a single small market

selected_mechanism.one_line_definition: The physical fuel-supply stack that decides whether any Railbelt AI data center can be powered: Cook Inlet gas is depleting, replacement fuel depends on which competing LNG-import terminal the RCA lets utilities recover infrastructure costs for, and on whether a data-center load's costs can be firewalled from existing ratepayers.

layers.name: Upstream gas supply (monopoly producer withdrawal)
layers.what_it_does: Sets the fuel-scarcity condition: Hilcorp (via Harvest) declined in May 2022 to renew long-term Cook Inlet gas contracts; Cook Inlet is projected to run out of gas ~2033, and Chugach's Hilcorp supply contract ends in 2028.
layers.controlling_actor: Hilcorp Alaska / Harvest Alaska (dominant Cook Inlet gas producer)

layers.name: LNG import terminal (physical replacement-fuel chokepoint)
layers.what_it_does: Three competing import proposals contend to supply replacement fuel — CEA/Harvest-Hilcorp refurbishing the Nikiski export terminal, Enstar/Glenfarne a new facility tied to Alaska LNG (pipeline claimed 2029), and Cook Inlet Energy a floating Osprey-platform facility — but only one can be economically justified for one small market.
layers.controlling_actor: Terminal developers (Glenfarne/Enstar; Harvest/CEA; Cook Inlet Energy), gated by RCA cost recovery

layers.name: Railbelt utility generation
layers.what_it_does: Chugach Electric's Cook Inlet gas fell from ~30% of its fuel supply to under 1% last year; Chugach currently doesn't have enough natural gas to make the electricity needed by a large data center. GVEA faces the parallel Interior constraint.
layers.controlling_actor: Chugach Electric Association; Golden Valley Electric Association

layers.name: RCA cost-allocation / cross-subsidization gate (CHOKEPOINT)
layers.what_it_does: Under AS 42.05.141 the RCA sets just, fair, and reasonable rates and determines what infrastructure costs a utility may recover from ratepayers — so the RCA's binary approve/deny on cost recovery for a specific import terminal, and its rule on whether a data-center load must fully cover its cost of service, decides whether replacement fuel gets financed and whether members subsidize new AI load.
layers.controlling_actor: Regulatory Commission of Alaska (rate/cost-recovery authority under AS 42.05.141)

layers.name: Data-center demand (the AI load)
layers.what_it_does: Supplies the load that has to be fueled: the Department of the Air Force has invited AI companies to propose data centers on 4,700 acres across JBER, Eielson, and Clear, with twelve parcels identified for potential development.
layers.controlling_actor: Department of the Air Force / DoD (Request for Land-use Proposals) plus private developers

chokepoint.actor: Regulatory Commission of Alaska, acting under its AS 42.05.141 rate and cost-recovery authority
chokepoint.binary_decision: Grant or deny utility recovery of import-terminal infrastructure costs (and set whether a data-center load must fully cover its own cost of service) — a 3-2 binary-majority vote of one named body that determines which single terminal gets financed and whether AI load is firewalled from ratepayers.

selected_mechanism.structural_read: Cook Inlet's depletion has converted Railbelt fuel supply into a natural-monopoly build: the market is too small to justify more than one LNG-import terminal, so the RCA's cost-recovery decision is the real switch on whether any replacement fuel exists at all. That makes the RCA — not the terminal developers, not the utilities, not the Air Force — the layer that reprices the entire AI-data-center power question. First gas is not before 2028-2029, which means firm fuel is the binding constraint on Alaska data-center siting, ahead of interconnection or permitting.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: A developer or PM evaluating a Railbelt AI/data-center site this week should treat firm-fuel availability (an RCA-approved LNG-import terminal delivering first gas 2028-2029), not land or interconnection, as the gating milestone — and should assume, per Chugach's stated position, that the load will be required to fully cover its own cost of service rather than ride existing ratepayers.
selected_mechanism.ak_consequence: Facilities/power: the DAF 4,700-acre, 12-parcel AI data-center program at JBER/Eielson/Clear and Chugach's data-center inquiries cannot secure firm Railbelt power until the RCA approves cost recovery for one Cook Inlet LNG-import terminal delivering first gas ~2028-2029.

_validation_note: Selected F1 at MEDIUM confidence with two honest caveats. (1) Gate 5: the chokepoint is the five-member Regulatory Commission of Alaska. This is the permissible binary-majority of one named body (a docketed 3-2 grant/deny cost-recovery vote under AS 42.05.141), not a diffuse 'the agency' veto — and it is reinforced by a genuine structural asymmetry (only one LNG-import terminal is economically justifiable for one small market) — but it is the weaker single-actor form and is scored accordingly. (2) Gate 3: the load-bearing chokepoint layer (RCA rate/cost-recovery authority) IS anchored to a primary statute (AS 42.05.141, re-fetched via FindLaw). The other four layers are anchored to reputable, re-fetched journalism (alaskaenergy.org, ADN, Air & Space Forces) rather than agency primaries because every agency-primary host attempted this run was blocked — rca.alaska.gov (403), chugachelectric.com (404), sam.gov (unfetchable), defense.gov/war.gov (redirect, no content), glenfarne.com (503), gasline.alaska.gov (DNS failure). The structure is multiply corroborated and non-confabulated (two independent outlets name the same actors; the AI tie is DIRECT, not inferential — ADN May 5: Chugach Electric currently doesn't have enough natural gas to make the electricity needed by a large data center), so the source-tier mixing is disclosed rather than treated as a fabrication. Overlap rule applied: F1 (fuel-supply/import-terminal side) is distinct from the already-anatomized May 20 Railbelt interconnection chain and the Jun 24 NMFS Cook Inlet offshore chain. The verbatim trigger span was confirmed present on the live June 23 page. Window NOT broadened; a defensible target cleared all seven gates at 14 days.
